Fever, Rash and Joint Pain: Name the Rash, Then Date the Exposure

Hives mid-course of an antibiotic, or a face-first pink rash in the unvaccinated

DiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line
  • Itchy hives, low fever, nodes and tender but unswollen joints 5 to 14 days into a drug (penicillins, cefaclor, TMP-SMX (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole)): serum sickness-like reaction. Stop the drug; it resolves. More common in children than serum sickness, and milder.
  • Same timing after a foreign protein (antivenom, antitoxin, monoclonal antibody), with high fever and low complement: serum sickness.
  • Fine pink rash from face to feet within 24 hours, palms and soles spared, posterior auricular and suboccipital nodes, unvaccinated and well: rubella. In teenage girls and women, finger and wrist pain may last up to a month.
  • Swollen, hot, migratory joints, carditis or erythema marginatum 2 to 4 weeks after an untreated sore throat: rheumatic fever (extremely rare after prompt penicillin).

Sexual history decides two rashes: pustules with tenosynovitis (gonococcus) and a rash on the palms and soles (secondary syphilis).

Diagnosis
Name the rash
DiagnosisRashTell
Serum sickness-like reactionItchy hives lasting over 24 hours; mucosa sparedTender, unswollen joints; nodes; mild proteinuria possible
RubellaFine pink maculopapular, face to feet within 24 hours; palms, soles sparedLow fever; posterior auricular, suboccipital nodes
MeaslesFace first, spreads over days, confluentFever 40 °C or more; cough, coryza, conjunctivitis; ill; no joint pain
VaricellaItchy vesicles in cropsNo joint pain
EBV (Epstein-Barr virus)Mainly after a beta-lactamExudative pharyngitis; posterior nodes
Disseminated gonococcal infectionA few painless vesiculopustules on distal limbs, rarely the faceTenosynovitis and migratory joint pain, or one hot, swollen knee; sexually active
Secondary syphilisMaculopapular, including palms and solesGeneralized nodes, condylomata lata
Acute rheumatic feverErythema marginatum: faint, non-itchy pink rings with clear centers, trunkSwollen, hot, migratory large joints; carditis
Scarlet feverSandpaper papules, flexural linesWith the sore throat; strawberry tongue
IgA (immunoglobulin A) vasculitisPalpable purpura, buttocks and legsNormal platelets; abdominal pain; hematuria
Stevens-Johnson syndromePainful dusky macules that blister, days to weeks into a drugHemorrhagic oral erosions; skin hurts rather than itches
Management and treatment
By situation Serum sickness-like reaction – stop the drug if still taken; antihistamine and NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs); avoid the drug afterward; epinephrine only for airway, breathing or blood-pressure compromise · Rubella – supportive care, NSAIDs for the joints; keep away from pregnant contacts (miscarriage, stillbirth, congenital rubella syndrome)
Practice
  1. 6-year-old boy, 2 days of fever, itchy spreading rash sore wrists and ankles strep throat 9 days ago; oral penicillin ends tomorrow Hives on arms and back T 38.8 °C · nodes: neck, axillae, groin · joints tender, not swollen or red → Serum sickness-like reaction → hives with tender, unswollen joints and nodes 5 to 14 days into a drug is a serum sickness-like reaction: stop the penicillin; rheumatic fever has swollen migratory joints and is extremely rare after treated strep, and scarlet fever has no hives or joint pain
  2. 16-year-old girl, unvaccinated, pink maculopapular rash since yesterday face first, now trunk, limbs; palms, soles spared finger, wrist pain since this morning; tired; no stiff neck inconsistent condom use Postauricular, suboccipital nodes; clear throat T 38.2 °C · well · rash blanches → Rubella virus → a fine rash from face to limbs within a day, sparing palms and soles, with posterior auricular and suboccipital nodes and finger arthralgia in an unvaccinated, well teenager is rubella; gonococcal pustules rarely reach the face, and measles makes the patient ill with cough, coryza and conjunctivitis, without joint pain
  3. 14-year-old boy, 10 days after antivenom for a rattlesnake bite urticarial rash for 2 days knee and wrist pain, worse with movement Feels unwell; no wheeze or lip swelling T 39.5 °C · urine protein 2+ · serum complement low → Serum sickness → high fever, hives, joint pain and low complement 5 to 14 days after a foreign protein is serum sickness: immune complexes against the antivenom
  4. 7-year-old girl on day 8 of amoxicillin for otitis media 1 day of itchy wheals on trunk, limbs ankle and wrist pain, worse with movement; joints not swollen No wheeze; lips and tongue normal T 38.1 °C · blood pressure normal → Stop amoxicillin and give an oral antihistamine → a serum sickness-like reaction: stop the amoxicillin and give an oral antihistamine; epinephrine only for airway, breathing or blood-pressure compromise
  5. 11-year-old boy with 5 days of fever hot, swollen right knee, then left elbow as the knee settles sore throat 3 weeks ago, not treated Faint, non-itchy pink rings with clear centers on trunk T 38.6 °C · ASO titer elevated → Acute rheumatic fever → migratory polyarthritis and erythema marginatum 2 to 4 weeks after untreated pharyngitis, with strep evidence, is acute rheumatic fever; Lyme arthritis is a single large joint months after erythema migrans
  6. 17-year-old girl, 3 days of fever pain over the backs of both wrists and hands with finger extension painful, swollen right knee Five small pustules on forearms and ankles T 38.4 °C · sexually active, no condoms · vaccinations up to date → Disseminated gonococcal infection → tenosynovitis, a few pustules and a swollen knee in a sexually active teen is disseminated gonococcal infection: aspirate the knee, NAAT of genital, pharyngeal and rectal sites, blood cultures, then ceftriaxone
  7. 15-year-old girl, never vaccinated, with a fine pink rash began on the face; reached the legs within a day palms and soles spared; sore finger joints Suboccipital nodes; oropharynx clear T 38.0 °C · no conjunctivitis or cough → Rubella IgM serology → a face-to-feet rash within a day with suboccipital nodes and finger arthralgia in an unvaccinated teen is rubella: confirm with rubella IgM
  8. 5-year-old boy who finished amoxicillin for otitis media 6 days ago raised, nonblanching purple spots on buttocks and legs painful, swollen ankles Colicky abdominal pain T 37.9 °C · platelet count normal → IgA vasculitis → palpable purpura on the buttocks and legs with normal platelets, joint pain and colicky abdominal pain is IgA vasculitis, not a drug reaction: check a urinalysis
Pairs with Acute Rheumatic Fever: Jones criteria, the strep clock, and Lyme arthritis among its mimics. Bruising and Purpura in a Child: IgA vasculitis. Tick-Borne Fever and Rash: erythema migrans. Exanthems in a Child: rash and fever without joint pain. Genital Ulcer: Painless or Painful: the chancre before secondary syphilis. Anaphylaxis and Its Mimics: the minutes-not-days reaction.
Transferable rule

When a triad is shared, classify the most specific finding first (here the rash), then put it on a clock against the exposure.
